subject: Re: Request: Load experiment protocol + QPS / tail-latency evidence
messages:
From: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@acme.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: Load experiment protocol + QPS / tail-latency evidence

Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this RFP — Acme is compiling a set of performance proofs for our procurement packet. We have a short list of concrete evidence items we need to validate Redwood's claims around latency and throughput for text-generation workloads. Can you provide the following for the model variant you are proposing (open-model-8k / quantized variant if applicable):

1) A short runnable test protocol (steps + toolchain) we can reproduce.
2) Steady-state throughput (qps per GPU) at nominal prompt mix and context length.
3) Latency distributions: p50, p95, p99, p99.9 for token-level and response-level (end-to-end).
4) Cold-start variability (time from idle to first-token p95/p99).
5) Behavior under autoscale and graceful degradation: what happens at 1.5x and 2x provisioned load?
6) Any differences when KV / prefix caching is enabled (session workloads).
7) Test artifacts: run logs, aggregated CSV, and the exact load script you ran.

We are trying to produce a reproducible appendix; please attach small sample CSVs and the YAML/JS load script. If there are constraints on instance types / driver versions we need to reproduce the experiment, list them.

Best,
Liam
Procurement — Acme Systems

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@acme.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-20T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Load experiment protocol + QPS / tail-latency evidence

Hi Liam — thanks, this is great context. Below is a concise, reproducible summary and the artifacts are attached. We're happy to schedule a short run-through with your engineering team.

Summary of the runs we attached (quantized variant unless noted):
- Test harness: custom load-runner (open-source) + Redis-based warm cache shim; closed-loop driver to maintain target QPS and avoid queue buildup. See attached loadscript YAML for exact params.
- Hardware used: 1x A100-80GB equivalent (shared pool for Hosted/Dedicated test); CUDA 12.1, driver 535.xx, Triton runtime 2.4.*.
- Prompt mix: 70% short (<=64 tokens), 30% long (512-1024 tokens); average response length 120 tokens.
- Warmup: 10-minute warmup, then 60-minute steady-state.

Key steady-state numbers (single-GPU, quantized 4-bit variant, 8k KV cache disabled):
- Target steady QPS: 300 qps (per GPU) sustained at the prompt mix above.
- Response-latency (end-to-end, generation complete): p50=24 ms, p95=72 ms, p99=170 ms, p99.9=360 ms.
- Token emission p99.9 measured at 42 ms per token on the same runs (useful for streaming scenarios).

Cold-start (idle -> first token) observed during the same harness: p50=85 ms, p95=240 ms, p99=480 ms (this reflects model kernel initialization + memory population; reduced with pre-warmed pool).

Autoscale/graceful degradation behavior:
- At 1.5x provisioned load (450 qps target) we observe elevated queuing; p99 rises ~2.2x vs steady-state and error rate remains <0.35% with our backpressure.
- At 2x (600 qps) we enter controlled shedding: prioritized short responses, model fallbacks to a lower-cost quantized shard (reduction in quality measured; we can provide evaluation deltas). Error rate climbs to ~1.8% and p99.9 can exceed 1s during peak spikes. We recommend canarying anything above 1.5x.

KV/prefix cache impact (session workloads): enabling prefix caching for repeated conversational contexts increased effective throughput by ~38% for our trace (cache hit-rate ~46%) and reduced p99 by ~45 ms. We include a CSV with per-run cache hit rates.

Attached artifacts (truncated):
- acme-qps-summary-20270121.csv — per-run percentiles, QPS, CPU/GPU utilization snapshots.
- 20270120-kp-loadscript.yml — the exact YAML driver we ran that builds on our open load-runner.
- runbook-observability-snippets.txt — the Prometheus/Grafana queries we used to compute percentiles.

Methodology notes (short):
- Closed-loop driver to maintain target QPS; windowed sampling of latencies to avoid tail amplification from cold-running events.
- Each steady-state includes a 10-minute warmup; we compute percentiles on the subsequent 50 minutes.
- We don't inject synthetic failures by default (we can run preemption / spot interrupts on request).

Let us know which additional variants you want (non-quantized, larger context lengths, or multi-GPU sharded runs) and we can produce the CSVs. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk through the run artifacts and reproduce a short run with your team.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Attachments: acme-qps-summary-20270121.csv (csv), 20270120-kp-loadscript.yml (text), runbook-observability-snippets.txt (txt)
